facts.text: Newtown is located in central Dillon County, sitting just south of the county seat with continuous development between the two communities.
Economic expansion in Newtown during the 1920s and 1940s was closely tied to the tobacco industry and enhanced railroad infrastructure.
Newtown remained predominantly African American into the late 20th century, with local institutions emerging to serve the community during economic transitions.
The terrain around Newtown is characteristically flat, reflecting the lowlands of the Pee Dee River basin with an average elevation of 112 feet.
Newtown's climate supports a growing season of approximately 217 days, which is highly conducive to agriculture in the surrounding Pee Dee region.
Early land use in the Newtown region centered on small-scale farming of cotton and tobacco using modest wooden structures on brick piers.
